cards.title: Never share an OTP
facts: An OTP works like a one-time key to an account.
Banks, apps and companies never ask you to share an OTP.
Scammers create urgency, prizes or fear to rush you.
do: Never share an OTP with anyone
dont: Don't share OTPs, even with 'customer care'
Don't click links in prize messages

myths.statement: It's safe to share an OTP with someone who says they're from your bank.
myths.truth: Banks never ask for OTPs. Anyone asking is a scammer.

quiz.q: Someone calls saying they're from a gaming company and asks for the OTP sent to your parent's phone. You…
options: Hang up and tell your parent
quiz.explanation: OTPs are never shared. Tell a parent right away.

scams.text: 🎁 Congrats! You won 10,000 free coins! Enter your parent's phone number and the OTP you receive to claim now. Offer ends in 5 minutes!
scams.explanation: Scam! Nobody gives free coins for an OTP. Close it and tell an adult.

scams.text: Your OTP for login is 482910. Do NOT share this OTP with anyone. Bank staff will never ask for it.
scams.explanation: This looks like a genuine OTP message: it warns you not to share it and doesn't ask you to do anything. Only use it if you started the login yourself.

situations: {name} is playing an online game {at} when a pop-up offers free coins. It asks for the OTP sent to {name}'s mother's phone. {relation} says 'Quick, everyone's doing it!'
scenario.question: What should {name} do?

rubric.note: An OTP is a key to the account.

rubric.point: Tell a parent or trusted adult
rubric.note: Adults can check and report it.

cards.title: Bill, KYC and prize scams
facts: Scam messages often come from personal mobile numbers and threaten disconnection or account blocking.
Official companies ask you to use their official app or website.
do: Check bills only on the official app or website
dont: Don't call numbers from threatening SMS
Don't install apps a caller asks you to install

myths.statement: If a message has your name in it, it must be genuine.
myths.truth: Scammers often have names from leaked data. Check through official apps.

quiz.q: Which is a warning sign of a scam message?
options: Urgent threat with a personal phone number
A bill you already paid in the app
quiz.explanation: Urgency + personal number + threat = classic scam pattern.

scams.text: Dear customer, your electricity will be disconnected tonight at 9:30 PM as your last bill was not updated. Please call electricity officer immediately on 98•••• 4417.
scams.explanation: Scam. Electricity companies don't send threats from personal mobile numbers. Check the bill in the official app and report to 1930.

scams.text: Your bank KYC expires today! Update now at bit.ly/kyc-upd8 or your account will be BLOCKED within 2 hours.
scams.explanation: Scam. Short links, threats and deadlines are red flags. Banks ask you to visit the branch or the official app.

cards.title: Strong passwords
facts: Long passphrases are harder to guess than short complex passwords.
Reusing one password means one leak opens every account.
Two-step verification blocks most account takeovers.
do: Use different passwords for important accounts
dont: Don't share passwords, even with best friends
Don't use your name or birthday

myths.statement: It's fine to share your password with your best friend.
myths.truth: Friendships change, and phones get lost. Keep passwords private (parents can help).

quiz.explanation: Long passphrases of random words are strong and easy to remember.

cards.title: Strangers and privacy online
facts: People online may not be who they say they are.
School name, address and uniform photos can reveal where you are.
do: Tell a trusted adult if someone makes you uncomfortable
dont: Don't share your address, school or live location
Never agree to meet an online friend alone

myths.statement: If someone online knows your favourite game, they must be your age.
myths.truth: Anyone can pretend. Keep personal details private and tell an adult.

quiz.q: A gaming friend asks which school you go to. You…
options: Don't share, and tell an adult if they keep asking

situations: {name} has been chatting with a 'gamer friend' for weeks. Today the friend asks for a photo in school uniform and suggests meeting {at} without telling parents.
scenario.question: What should {name} do?

rubric.point: Don't send photos or personal details

rubric.note: 'Don't tell your parents' is a big warning sign.

rubric.point: Tell a parent or trusted adult
